question: What type of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to stop outside air from rushing in when doors open?
explanation: Positive pressure acts like an invisible shield, pushing air outward when doors open so germs stay out of the sterile theatre. Well done! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why do theatres carefully monitor room temperature and humidity during surgery?

options.A: To make the room comfortable for visitors and family members
options.B: To ensure surgical instruments do not rust during the procedure
options.C: To discourage bacterial growth and prevent patient hypothermia
options.D: To keep the anesthesia machine running at peak efficiency

explanation: Controlling the climate stops bacteria from multiplying and protects the patient's body heat while they are under anesthesia. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h1)

question: In which zone of the surgical suite are hospital staff still allowed to wear regular street clothes?
explanation: The unrestricted zone is the front area where you enter and receive patients before changing into your fresh theatre scrubs. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h2)

question: When must you wear a surgical mask while working in the surgical suite?

options.A: In the unrestricted zone when greeting incoming patients and families
options.B: Whenever staff members feel unwell or have a mild cough
options.C: In the restricted zone where sterile supplies and procedures are located
options.D: Only when the surgeon is actively making an incision on the patient

explanation: Masks protect the sterile field from mouth and nose droplets, so they are mandatory inside the restricted zone at all times. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h2)

question: As an unsterile team member, what is the minimum safe distance you must keep from a sterile field?
explanation: Always stay at least one foot away! This simple rule stops you from accidentally brushing against or contaminating sterile items. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h3)

question: What should you do if you spot an item on the sterile table and you are not totally sure if it is sterile?

options.A: Consider it contaminated and remove it from the field immediately
options.B: Ask the surgeon if it looks clean enough to use anyway
options.C: Wipe the item down with an alcohol swab and place it back
options.D: Leave it alone until the end of the surgical procedure

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! The golden rule of theatre asepsis is that if sterility is questionable, the item is dirty. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h3)

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the rinse water flow off your arms?

options.A: From the hands down toward the elbows
options.B: Directly off the side of the wrists
options.C: From the forearms up to the palms
options.D: From the elbows up toward the fingertips

explanation: Always let water flow from clean (hands) to less clean (elbows). This prevents dirty water from running back down onto your freshly washed fingers! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which parts of a sterile surgical gown are considered safe to touch as a sterile team member?

options.A: The neckline and the inner ties used to secure the back closure
options.B: The chest area down to the table level and the sleeves from above the elbow to the cuffs
options.C: The entire back of the gown from the shoulders all the way down to the hemline
options.D: The lower skirt of the gown below the level of the sterile instrument table

explanation: Remember: only the front from chest to table level and the sleeves are sterile. The back of the gown is always considered unsterile! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h4)

question: At what exact moment during theatre proceedings is the 'Time Out' safety check done?

options.A: As soon as the patient enters the unrestricted hospital reception area
options.B: Just before the surgical dressings and bandages are applied
options.C: While the patient is waking up in the post-anesthesia care unit
options.D: Immediately before the surgical skin incision is made

explanation: The Time Out is a mandatory quick pause right before cutting, allowing the whole team to double-check the patient, site, and procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using the surgical safety checklist in the operating room?

options.A: To evaluate the clinical performance of junior medical students
options.B: To prevent wrong-site surgery and reduce preventable surgical errors
options.C: To speed up the turnover time between consecutive surgical cases
options.D: To ensure the hospital insurance policy covers the surgical fees

explanation: Communication saves lives! The checklist keeps everyone on the same page so mistakes are caught before they happen. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h5)

question: How should you apply antiseptic skin prep solution to a patient's surgical site?

options.A: In a random zig-zag pattern across the entire torso and limbs
options.B: Starting at the incision site and moving outward in circles
options.C: Starting at the outer edges and scrubbing inward to the center
options.D: Using a back-and-forth motion right over the planned incision

explanation: Always move from clean to dirty! Starting at the incision and working outward ensures you don't drag skin bacteria into the clean cut. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is a key responsibility when positioning a patient for an operation?

options.A: Leaving all joints uncovered so they can move freely during prep
options.B: Padding bony prominences to prevent pressure sores and nerve injury
options.C: Tying the patient tightly to the operating table with heavy restraints
options.D: Ensuring the patient's head hangs lower than the body at all times

explanation: Patients lie still for a long time under anesthesia, so careful padding protects their joints, skin, and nerves from damage. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which two theatre team members are primarily responsible for performing surgical counts?
explanation: The scrub nurse and circulating nurse team up to carefully count and record all instruments, sponges, and needles used. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is the immediate correct action if a surgical sponge count is incorrect at the end of a surgery?

options.A: Assume the package count was wrong at the factory and ignore it
options.B: Document the missing sponge in the chart and finish closing quickly
options.C: Stop closure immediately and search the wound and room until found
options.D: Order an x-ray for tomorrow morning after the patient wakes up

explanation: Never rush past a bad count! Closing must pause immediately so a full search can be done to ensure no item is left inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe safety practice in the operating room?

options.A: Using smoke evacuation systems for electrosurgical units
options.B: Disposing of used scalpel blades in puncture-resistant containers
options.C: Wearing protective eyewear to shield against blood splashes
options.D: Recapping used injection needles by hand before disposal

explanation: Never recap needles with both hands! It is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries and is strictly discouraged. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h8)

question: Why do theatres use smoke evacuation systems during surgeries that involve burning or cutting tissue with electrical devices?

options.A: To keep the operating room temperature from rising too high
options.B: To ensure the surgeon can see the blood vessels more clearly
options.C: To remove toxic smoke plumes and viral particles from the air
options.D: To prevent the fire alarm system from going off in the hospital

explanation: Electrical surgical tools create smoke containing harmful chemicals and tiny biological particles that theatre staff shouldn't breathe in. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h8)
